title: Ordinary tensor construction and universal derived cohomology transport
statement: For compatible coefficient equivalences eR:R0≃R and eB:B0≃B and universal left-derived scalar-extension functors L0,L [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], [def-weil-module-base-change], fix degree i. The four rings are commutative in a common universe, with algebra structures R0→B0 and R→B; derived categories for R0,B0 and R,B may have distinct morphism universes. Their counits ε0,ε have the universal left-derived property for ordinary scalar extension. Compatibility means eB composed with R0→B0 equals R→B composed with eR. Write V for termwise restriction along eR, U for restriction along eB, T0,T for termwise ordinary extension to B0,B, and P0,P for complex localization followed by L0,L and degree-i homology. For each complex, c0,c are the homology maps of the respective counits composed with the derived and homotopy homology factorization isomorphisms. There exist natural isomorphisms t:V⋙T0≅T⋙U_complex and d:V⋙P0≅P⋙U. The ordinary map t sends b⊗x to eB(b)⊗x, and d intertwines c0,c through H^i(t) and the exact-restriction homology isomorphism. Neither an extra algebra nor a cohomology model is required.

proof.text: Use hRB to view eB as an eR-semilinear equivalence. TensorProduct.congr with the identity semilinear equivalence from an R-module restricted along eR gives an additive tensor equivalence. Tensor induction proves B0-linearity. Its pure-tensor formula proves naturality, yielding the ordinary module functor isomorphism.

Apply the module natural isomorphism termwise to get t and its generator equation. Apply exists_derivedExtension_ringEquiv_counit to t and that equation, obtaining d and the counit square. Package the two isomorphisms and their properties.

theorem exists_derivedExtension_ringEquiv_cohomology
    {R₀ B₀ R B : Type u}
    [CommRing R₀] [CommRing B₀] [CommRing R] [CommRing B]
    [Algebra R₀ B₀] [Algebra R B]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} R₀)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (ModuleCat.{u} B₀)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (ModuleCat.{u} R)]
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w'} (ModuleCat.{u} B)]
    (L₀ : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R₀) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B₀))
    (L : DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} R) ⥤ DerivedCategory (ModuleCat.{u} B))
    (ε₀ : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ L₀ ⟶
      (extendScalars (algebraMap R₀ B₀)).mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh)
    (ε : DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ L ⟶
      (extendScalars (algebraMap R B)).mapHomotopyCategory (.up ℤ) ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh)
    (h₀ : L₀.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε₀ (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (.up ℤ)))
    (h : L.IsLeftDerivedFunctor ε (HomotopyCategory.quasiIso _ (.up ℤ)))
    (eR : R₀ ≃+* R) (eB : B₀ ≃+* B)
    (hRB : eB.toRingHom.comp (algebraMap R₀ B₀) =
      (algebraMap R B).comp eR.toRingHom) (i : ℤ) :
    let π₀ := HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat.{u} R₀) (.up ℤ)
    let π := HomotopyCategory.quotient (ModuleCat.{u} R) (.up ℤ)
    let H₀ := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} B₀) i
    let H := DerivedCategory.homologyFunctor (ModuleCat.{u} B) i
    let P₀ := π₀ ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ L₀ ⋙ H₀
    let P := π ⋙ DerivedCategory.Qh ⋙ L ⋙ H
    let V := (restrictScalars.{u} eR.toRingHom).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let U := restrictScalars.{u} eB.toRingHom
    let T₀ := (extendScalars (algebraMap R₀ B₀)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let T := (extendScalars (algebraMap R B)).mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)
    let c₀ := fun K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R₀) ℤ ↦
      H₀.map (ε₀.app (π₀.obj K)) ≫
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactorsh (ModuleCat.{u} B₀) i).hom.app
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj (T₀.obj K)) ≫
        (HomotopyCategory.homologyFunctorFactors (ModuleCat.{u} B₀) (.up ℤ) i).hom.app
          (T₀.obj K)
    let c := fun K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ ↦
      H.map (ε.app (π.obj K)) ≫
        (DerivedCategory.homologyFunctorFactorsh (ModuleCat.{u} B) i).hom.app
          ((HomotopyCategory.quotient _ _).obj (T.obj K)) ≫
        (HomotopyCategory.homologyFunctorFactors (ModuleCat.{u} B) (.up ℤ) i).hom.app
          (T.obj K)
    ∃ (t : V ⋙ T₀ ≅ T ⋙ U.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ))
      (d : V ⋙ P₀ ≅ P ⋙ U),
      (∀ (K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) (j : ℤ) (b : B₀) (x : K.X j),
        (t.hom.app K).f j (b ⊗ₜ[R₀,algebraMap R₀ B₀] x) =
          eB b ⊗ₜ[R,algebraMap R B] x) ∧
      ∀ K : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ,
        d.hom.app K ≫ U.map (c K) =
          c₀ (V.obj K) ≫ HomologicalComplex.homologyMap (t.hom.app K) i ≫
            ((T.obj K).sc i |>.mapHomologyIso U).hom
